an9.36:1.1: “I tell you, the ending of the effluents depends on the first jhāna…
an9.36:1.5: the dimension of the infinitude of space…
an9.36:1.6: the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness…
an9.36:1.8: I tell you, the ending of the effluents depends on the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.
an9.36:2.1: “‘I tell you, the ending of the effluents depends on the first jhāna.’ Thus it has been said.
an9.36:2.2: In reference to what was it said?
an9.36:2.3: There is the case where a monk, quite secluded from sensuality, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters & remains in the first jhāna: rapture & pleasure born of seclusion, accompanied by directed thought & evaluation.
an9.36:2.4: He regards whatever phenomena there that are connected with form, feeling, perception, fabrications, & consciousness, as inconstant, stressful, a disease, a cancer, an arrow, painful, an affliction, alien, a disintegration, an emptiness, not-self.
an9.36:2.5: He turns his mind away from those phenomena and,
an9.36:2.6: having done so, inclines his mind to the property of deathlessness:
an9.36:2.7: ‘This is peace, this is exquisite—the pacification of all fabrications; the relinquishing of all acquisitions; the ending of craving; dispassion; cessation; unbinding.’
an9.36:3.1: “Suppose that an archer or archer’s apprentice were to practice on a straw man or mound of clay, so that after a while he would become able to shoot long distances, to fire accurate shots in rapid succession, and to pierce great masses.
an9.36:3.2: In the same way, there is the case where a monk… enters & remains in the first jhāna: rapture & pleasure born of seclusion, accompanied by directed thought & evaluation.
an9.36:3.3: He regards whatever phenomena there that are connected with form, feeling, perception, fabrications, & consciousness, as inconstant, stressful, a disease, a cancer, an arrow, painful, an affliction, alien, a disintegration, an emptiness, not-self.
an9.36:3.4: He turns his mind away from those phenomena and,
an9.36:3.5: having done so, inclines his mind to the property of deathlessness:
an9.36:3.6: ‘This is peace, this is exquisite—the pacification of all fabrications; the relinquishing of all acquisitions; the ending of craving; dispassion; cessation; unbinding.’
an9.36:3.7: “Staying right there, he reaches the ending of the effluents.
an9.36:3.8: Or, if not, then—through this very Dhamma-passion, this Dhamma-delight, and from the total ending of the five lower fetters [self-identification views, grasping at habits & practices, uncertainty, sensual passion, and irritation]—he is due to arise spontaneously (in the Pure Abodes), there to be totally unbound, never again to return from that world.
an9.36:3.9: “‘I tell you, the ending of the effluents depends on the first jhāna.’
an9.36:3.10: Thus it was said, and in reference to this was it said.

an9.36:6.1: “‘I tell you, the ending of the effluents depends on the dimension of the infinitude of space.’ Thus it has been said.
an9.36:6.2: In reference to what was it said?
an9.36:6.3: There is the case where a monk—with the complete transcending of perceptions of (physical) form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, and not attending to perceptions of multiplicity, (perceiving,) ‘Infinite space’—enters & remains in the dimension of the infinitude of space.
an9.36:6.4: He regards whatever phenomena there that are connected with feeling, perception, fabrications, & consciousness, as inconstant, stressful, a disease, a cancer, an arrow, painful, an affliction, alien, a disintegration, an emptiness, not-self.
an9.36:6.5: He turns his mind away from those phenomena and,
an9.36:6.6: having done so, inclines his mind to the property of deathlessness:
an9.36:6.7: ‘This is peace, this is exquisite—the pacification of all fabrications; the relinquishing of all acquisitions; the ending of craving; dispassion; cessation; unbinding.’

an9.36:7.4: there to be totally unbound, never again to return from that world.
an9.36:7.5: “‘I tell you, the ending of the effluents depends on the dimension of the infinitude of space.’
an9.36:7.6: Thus it was said, and in reference to this was it said.

an9.36:10.1: “Thus, as far as the perception-attainments go, that is as far as gnosis-penetration goes.
an9.36:10.3: the attainment of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception & the attainment of the cessation of perception & feeling—I tell you that they are to be rightly explained by those monks who are meditators, skilled at attainment, skilled at attainment-emergence, who have attained & emerged in dependence on them.”
